what_it_does: Designing a neural network (such as an image-recognizing model) and the custom chip that runs it is usually done in two separate steps, which takes a very long time and often produces a mediocre result. UniCoS speeds this up by replacing slow training-based accuracy estimates with a proxy that scores a candidate network design in seconds — no actual training required. It also uses a clustering trick to quickly scan a wide variety of chip layouts (called dataflows, meaning the order in which the chip moves numbers through its math units), covering both CNN-style networks (which scan images with sliding filters) and Vision Transformer-style networks (which break images into patches and compare them with attention). The combined search finds good network-plus-chip pairs far faster than earlier methods.
